name: The 1787 chemical nomenclature
description: A collective French book proposed a systematic chemical naming scheme, together with a separately attributed system of chemical characters.

impact.note: A clearer, systematic language adopted by chemists across Europe; later chemical naming and notation descend from it. Depth could be argued as 2.

date.basis: Year is the date of the described episode in the cited source, not necessarily the invention or first conception.

events.statement: Guyton de Morveau, Lavoisier, Berthollet and Fourcroy published their nomenclature proposal in Paris.

evidence.supports: Attributes the naming proposal to four chemists, separately identifies authors of accompanying chemical characters, and records Paris 1787.

caveats: Hassenfratz and Adet are credited for accompanying chemical characters. The historical book is represented through library catalog and contents, not independently read in full. The proposal developed from earlier naming reforms.
